 AMIODARONE (PROCOR)

o: AMIODARONE (PROCOR)
FUROSAMIDE (FUSID)
APIXABAN (ELIQUIS)
ECITRALOPAM (CIPRALEX)
explanation:
After a fall on the way to the bathroom, distinguish impaired alertness or standing circulation from a drug that makes an injury more dangerous. **Apixaban primarily increases bleeding after trauma.**

**A. Amiodarone** — Bradycardia or conduction slowing can cause presyncope and a fall.
**B. Furosemide** — Diuresis can contribute to volume depletion and a postural pressure drop. Urgency also matters on the nighttime trip to the toilet.
**C. Apixaban** — Factor Xa inhibition affects clotting. It makes bleeding after a head strike an important concern without acting as a sedative or pressure-lowering drug.
**D. Escitalopram** — This SSRI belongs to a group of centrally acting drugs associated with falls. Review concomitant hypnotic use as well.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 634–636 and 666–669.

q: A 78-year-old man with chronic kidney disease and stable normocytic anemia is being evaluated. Nutritional deficiencies have not yet been assessed. What should be done before attributing the anemia to kidney disease and choosing treatment?
o: Begin an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent on the basis of the kidney-disease diagnosis
Proceed to blood transfusion on the basis of a complaint of fatigue
Check iron studies, ferritin, and vitamin B12 as part of the evaluation
Classify the finding as unexplained anemia of the elderly before further investigation
explanation:
Chronic kidney disease can impair the erythropoietin response, but a second treatable cause can coexist. A normal mean cell volume can occur with iron deficiency.

**Check iron studies, ferritin and vitamin B12 before assigning the anemia to kidney disease.**

**A. Start an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent.** An agent that stimulates marrow production will not replenish deficient iron or B12.
**B. Transfuse for fatigue.** Fatigue alone in a stable patient does not identify the mechanism or an urgent need for red cells.
**C. Assess iron and B12.** These tests can uncover a reversible deficiency that changes treatment even in someone with established kidney disease.
**D. Call the anemia unexplained.** That designation requires an evaluation for nutritional, renal, inflammatory and marrow causes.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1480.
ref: Hazzard Ch 94 — AGING OF THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM AND ANEMIA
chapterTitle: AGING OF THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM AND ANEMIA

q: A 78-year-old woman with recurrent urinary tract infections, pelvic organ prolapse, and stress incontinence says these problems have stopped her sexual activity. She lives alone but has a romantic partner. Her urologist has recommended a pessary and pelvic floor therapy. Which approach best addresses her sexual concerns?
o: Recommend accepting cessation of sexual activity as the expected outcome
Defer assessment of sexual concerns until prolapse surgery has been completed
Coordinate assessment of sexual concerns with treatment of the underlying conditions
Focus on the urinary symptoms and defer discussion of sexual distress
explanation:
Pelvic floor disorders can cause discomfort, leakage or distress during sex. **Coordinate treatment of prolapse and incontinence with assessment of her sexual goals**, including how proposed therapy fits her relationship.

**A. Accept cessation.** Stopping sexual activity need not be the expected outcome when modifiable barriers are present.
**B. Wait for surgery.** A pessary or pelvic floor therapy may help before surgery, and assessment can begin now.
**C. Coordinate care.** Discuss symptoms, desired intimacy and practical implications of the pessary and therapy.
**D. Treat urinary symptoms alone.** Urinary improvement may help, but it may leave her sexual discomfort or distress unresolved.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 521–522.
ref: Hazzard Ch 35 — SEXUALITY, SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING WOMAN

q: An 84-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment has recurrent falls, reduced activity, and increasing need for help with finances and medications. Examination shows bradykinesia, reduced arm swing, and a positive pull test. He takes metformin, lisinopril, and donepezil. Which assessment specifically investigates a possible blood-pressure or medication contribution to the falls?
o: Assess resting seated blood pressure and classify the gait abnormality
Measure muscle strength and assess the response to balance exercises
Assess brain imaging findings and classify the cognitive impairment
Measure orthostatic vital signs and review the medication regimen
explanation:
Falls in parkinsonism can reflect impaired postural reflexes, a drop in blood pressure on standing, or both. A normal pressure while seated can miss the drop that occurs when the patient gets up.

**Measure supine and standing vital signs and review the medicines.** Together these can show a postural fall in pressure and identify drugs that aggravate it.

**A. Seated pressure and gait classification.** A single position gives no comparison with standing. Gait assessment addresses a different contributor to falls.
**B. Strength and exercise response.** These assess muscle weakness or balance, not the circulatory response to standing.
**C. Imaging and cognitive classification.** Neither shows what happens to blood pressure when the patient stands.
**D. Orthostatic vital signs and medication review.** Relate any measured pressure drop to symptoms and to drugs that lower pressure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 672, 948, 1194.
ref: Hazzard Ch 61 — PARKINSON DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS

. Orthostatic vital signs and medication review.** Relate any measured pressure drop to symptoms and to drugs that lower pressure.

q: A woman with stress urinary incontinence has not improved sufficiently with conservative treatment and asks about duloxetine. How does Hazzard describe its role?
o: A second-line option in countries using it for stress incontinence
A first-line option preferred before behavioral treatment of stress incontinence
An option with US approval for treatment of stress incontinence
An option for urgency incontinence associated with atrophic vaginitis
explanation:
Duloxetine is a serotonin–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor used in some countries for stress incontinence. **It is a second-line option for selected patients who prefer medication to surgery.**

**A. A second-line option in countries using it for stress incontinence** — It can be considered after explaining likely benefit and adverse effects such as nausea or dry mouth.
**B. A first-line option preferred before behavioral treatment of stress incontinence** — Pelvic-floor training is the initial approach.
**C. An option with US approval for treatment of stress incontinence** — The United States has no FDA-approved drug indication for stress incontinence.
**D. An option for urgency incontinence associated with atrophic vaginitis** — Symptomatic vaginal atrophy is a different indication for local vaginal treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, pp. 713–714, Table 47-12.

q: An 81-year-old man with diabetes and peripheral neuropathy has worsening burning foot pain for three months. He takes metformin, lisinopril, and aspirin; HbA1c is 8.2%, and monofilament sensation is absent bilaterally. He lives alone and recently stopped driving because of pain. Gabapentin 300 mg three times daily caused severe dizziness. Which listed analgesic option belongs to the serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor class?
o: Pregabalin
Duloxetine
Amitriptyline
Capsaicin
explanation:
Different coanalgesics can treat burning diabetic pain by different mechanisms. **Duloxetine is the SNRI among these options.** Its suitability still depends on renal function, blood pressure and tolerability.

**A. Pregabalin** Pregabalin is a gabapentinoid. It can also cause dizziness and requires renal dose adjustment.
**B. Duloxetine** Duloxetine inhibits reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine, enhancing modulation of pain.
**C. Amitriptyline** Amitriptyline is a tricyclic with substantial anticholinergic effects.
**D. Capsaicin** Capsaicin is a topical treatment acting at TRPV1 on nociceptors.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Table 68-8, pp. 1063–1064.

. Amitriptyline** Amitriptyline is a tricyclic with substantial anticholinergic effects.

q: בן 78, מאובחן כשנה עם מחלת פרקינסון. סובל מנדודי שינה וסיוטים המופיעים בדרך כלל לפחות 90 דקות לאחר תחילת השינה. בנוסף, מתלונן על היעדר חוש ריח ועצי. רות מה הטיפול התרופתי המומלץ?
o: Brotizolam (Bondormin)
Melatonin (Circadin)
Zolpidem (Stilnox)
Zopiclone (Nocturno)
explanation:
Parkinson disease and episodes during probable REM sleep raise concern for REM sleep behavior disorder. Ask about witnessed dream enactment, because nightmares alone are insufficient. **Melatonin is the best-matched drug**, alongside measures to prevent injury.

**A. Brotizolam** This sedative does not specifically address RBD and can worsen balance and daytime alertness.
**B. Melatonin** Immediate-release melatonin is a treatment option for RBD associated with Parkinson disease.
**C. Zolpidem** A hypnotic for insomnia, it can cause confusion and complex behaviors during sleep.
**D. Zopiclone** Another hypnotic with sedative risks in older adults and no established role in treating dream enactment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 655. AASM RBD guideline (2023), recommendation 6. Gilat et al., Movement Disorders (2020), doi:10.1002/mds.27886.

Key note: The option names Circadin, a prolonged-release preparation. AASM supports immediate-release melatonin, and 4 mg prolonged-release melatonin did not reduce RBD events versus placebo in a small Parkinson disease trial.

. Zolpidem** A hypnotic for insomnia, it can cause confusion and complex behaviors during sleep.
. Zopiclone** Another hypnotic with sedative risks in older adults and no established role in treating dream enactment.

q: בן 82, דייר בבית אבות, מובא להערכה בעקבות אירועים חוזרים של "כמעט" איבוד הכרה. האירועים מתרחשים בדרך כלל כשעה לאחר הארוחות, ולעיתים מלוות בתחושת סחרחורת וחולשה. בהיסטוריה הרפואית: יתר לחץ דם, סוכרת סוג 2 ומחלת פרקינסון. בבדיקה גופנית בשכיבה – לחץ דם142/82מ"מ כספית, דופק 68 לדקה. מדידת לחץ דם שבוצעה 90 דקות לאחר ארוחת צהריים הדגימה לחץ דם סיסטולי של 118 מ"מ כספית. מהו המנגנון הפיזיולוגי העיקרי התורם לירידה בלחץ הדם לאחר הארוחה במטופל זה?
o: עלייה בפעילות מערכת העצבים הסימפתטית והתכווצות כלי דם היקפיים
עלייה בהחזר הוורידי ללב כתוצאה מספיגת נוזלים מהמעי
ירידה בהפרשת פפטידים מעיים כגון VIP ו- Neurotensin לאחר הארוחה
הצטברות דם במחזור הדם הספלנכני וכשל בהעלאת התנגודת כלי הדם
explanation:
Postprandial hypotension is a systolic drop of at least 20 mm Hg within two hours of starting a meal. The fall from 142 to 118 mm Hg at 90 minutes fits. **Splanchnic pooling combined with inadequate peripheral vasoconstriction** accounts for the fall.

**A. Increased sympathetic tone and vasoconstriction** — An effective rise in resistance defends blood pressure during digestion.
**B. Increased venous return** — This would improve cardiac filling. Pooling in the gut has the opposite immediate effect.
**C. Decreased gut-peptide secretion** — Release of vasoactive peptides after eating can promote vasodilation. Reduced secretion is not the principal mechanism here.
**D. Splanchnic pooling and failed resistance response** — Older age, diabetes and Parkinson disease can limit compensation for the redistribution of blood to the gut.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 668.

q: גבר בן 68 עם ירידה תחושתית-עצבית דו-צדדית ממושכת בשמיעה מדווח כי למרות שימוש עקבי במכשירי שמיעה מותאמים היטב, הוא עדיין מתקשה להבין דיבור אפילו בסביבה שקטה. בדיקת שמיעה מראה PTA4 של 70 דציבל באוזן הטובה יותר. הוא בריא ומעוניין לשפר את יכולת התקשורת שלו. מהי הפעולה המתאימה ביותר בשלב זה?
o: הגברת עוצמת ההגברה במכשירי השמיעה הקיימים
המלצה לעבור למכשירי שמיעה חזקים יותר מסוג אחר
המלצה להמשיך עם מכשירי השמיעה הנוכחיים ולהתמקד באסטרטגיות תקשורת
הפניה להערכה לקראת השתלת שתל שבלול
explanation:
A cochlear implant converts sound into electrical signals that stimulate the auditory nerve. **Refer this man for a cochlear implant evaluation.** Even his better ear has severe loss, and appropriately fitted hearing aids no longer give him usable speech understanding in quiet.

**A. Turn up the existing aids.** More volume can increase audibility without restoring the clarity needed to understand speech. His aids have already been fitted appropriately.
**B. Switch to a more powerful type.** Greater maximum output will not reliably overcome poor aided speech recognition. The audiogram and current aided performance warrant specialist evaluation.
**C. Continue the current aids and use communication strategies alone.** Facing the speaker and reducing noise remain helpful, but he struggles even in quiet. Those strategies alone leave an important rehabilitation option unexplored.
**D. Refer for cochlear implant evaluation.** PTA4 averages the thresholds at 500, 1000, 2000 and 4000 Hz. A value of 70 dB in his better ear, with inadequate aided communication, meets the clinical rationale for referral. The implant team evaluates candidacy, including aided speech performance.

Reference · Lin FR. Age-Related Hearing Loss. N Engl J Med 2024;390:1505–1512, pp1509–1511, Table 2 and Figure 2. doi:10.1056/NEJMcp2306778.

explanation:
**Homeostenosis is narrowing of physiologic reserve with age.** A person may function well at baseline but tolerate infection, dehydration or surgery poorly.

**A. Increased reserve.** This reverses the change. Capacity to compensate for stress generally narrows.
**B. Narrowing functional reserve.** A smaller disturbance can exceed the remaining reserve and cause functional decompensation.
**C. Abrupt isolated injury.** Homeostenosis develops gradually and can affect multiple organ systems.
**D. Change due only to disease.** Disease adds vulnerability, but age-related loss of reserve can occur without a discrete disease.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 576.

q: בן 88, מתגורר בביתו עם מטפלת צמודה. ברקע: מצב אחרי אירועי מוחי, דמנציה וסקולרית, אירועי אגיטציה בתדירות יומית. בהמלצת קלינאית תקשורת מוזן בכלכלה דייסתית. נבדק בחשד לדלקת ריאות כתוצאה מאספירציה. בבדיקתו: חום 38 מעלות, היגיינת פה ירודה, חרחורים לחים בבסיס ריאה ימנית. בצילום חזה תסנין בבסיס ריאה ימנית. מה מהבאים, במטופל זה, עשוי להפחית את הסיכון להתפתחות דלקת ראות כתוצאה מאספירציה?
o: הקפדה על היגיינת חלל הפה
מתן טיפול אנטי-פסיכוטי להרגעה לפני האוכל
החדרת צינור הזנה מסוג PEG
טיפול מונע ב- AMOXICILLIN
explanation:
Aspiration pneumonia can follow inhalation of saliva carrying oral bacteria. A puréed diet can change food handling while colonized secretions still reach the airway. **Regular oral hygiene may reduce pneumonia risk in this patient.**

**A. Care for the mouth and dentures** — Mechanical cleaning reduces the bacterial burden of material that can be aspirated. Adults at risk may benefit, although a trial in high-risk nursing home residents did not show a clear pneumonia reduction.
**B. Give an antipsychotic before eating** — Sedation can reduce attention during feeding. Antipsychotics can also impair swallowing through extrapyramidal effects.
**C. Insert a PEG tube** — Gastrostomy provides access for nutrition, but saliva and refluxed material can still be aspirated. A tube offers no reliable protection from aspiration pneumonia.
**D. Give preventive amoxicillin** — Antibiotics may be indicated for an established bacterial pneumonia. Routine amoxicillin does not correct dysphagia or substitute for daily oral care.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, ch. 31, p. 446, Table 31-5, and p. 451 · ch. 105, pp. 1690–1691.

q: מה מהבאים מהווה חלק מהבירור של פוליציטמיה?
o: בדיקת JAK4
Erythropoietin
Haptoglobin
RDW
keySource: IMA 2026-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q135
explanation:
Erythrocytosis can reflect autonomous marrow production or an external erythropoietin stimulus. **Measure serum erythropoietin (EPO)** to help distinguish the two mechanisms.

**A. JAK4 testing.** The relevant molecular test for suspected polycythemia vera is JAK2, not JAK4.
**B. Erythropoietin.** A low EPO supports autonomous erythropoiesis. An elevated EPO prompts evaluation for hypoxia or another secondary stimulus.
**C. Haptoglobin.** Haptoglobin is used primarily in evaluating hemolysis.
**D. RDW.** RDW measures variation in red-cell size. It is not the principal test for separating primary from secondary erythrocytosis.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 449, 451–452.

. Erythropoietin.** A low EPO supports autonomous erythropoiesis. An elevated EPO prompts evaluation for hypoxia or another secondary stimulus.
. Haptoglobin.** Haptoglobin is used primarily in evaluating hemolysis.
. RDW.** RDW measures variation in red-cell size. It is not the principal test for separating primary from secondary erythrocytosis.

explanationParts.text: Erythrocytosis can reflect autonomous marrow production or an external erythropoietin stimulus. **Measure serum erythropoietin (EPO)** to help distinguish the two mechanisms.
Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 449, 451–452.

chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 56 – Fluid and Electrolyte Disturbances
explanation:
Hyponatremia with urine osmolality around 100 mOsm/kg implies substantial vasopressin suppression and very dilute urine. **Polydipsia** is the best listed cause. A low-solute diet can produce a similar pattern, so history matters at this boundary.

**A. Polydipsia.** Water intake can exceed renal excretory capacity despite the kidney producing dilute urine.
**B. Hypothyroidism.** Severe hypothyroidism can impair water excretion, usually without near-maximal dilution during hyponatremia.
**C. Thiazide treatment.** Thiazides impair dilution and often increase urinary sodium during active exposure.
**D. Lung tumor.** Small-cell lung cancer can cause SIADH, which typically produces inappropriately concentrated urine rather than appropriate dilution.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 347–350.
